extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and researchers in enumerative combinatorics / discrete geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Theory and techniques for counting integer/rational points in polytopes (Ehrhart/quasipolynomials, reciprocity, volumes) and for counting walks/words via the transfer-matrix method (adjacency matrices, rational generating functions). Contains precise lemmas, propositions and worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomiality of H_n(r) (Proposition 4.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed n the function Hn(r) (the number of n×n N-matrices with every row and column sum r) is a polynomial in r of degree (n−1)^2. It satisfies symmetry/vanishing relations (zeros at specified integer points) and parity relations (functional equation relating Hn(−n−1−r) to Hn(r) up to a sign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses generating function Fn(λ) and rationality/denominator analysis; once polynomial degree is known, a finite number of integer values determine the polynomial (give method for computing Hn(r) by evaluating enough small r). Example: H3(r) determined from H3(0)=1 and H3(1)=6; small computed Fn(λ) values are supplied for illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of CF(E) for symmetric matrices (Lemma 4.6.3 / Lemma 4.6.1 consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the monoid E of symmetric n×n N-matrices with equal row/column sums, the completely fundamental elements CF(E) are contained in matrices of the form π or π+π^t where π is a permutation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterization underlies the rational form of generating functions for symmetric doubly-stochastic-type polytopes and yields constraints on denominators (denominators 1 or 2). Use to deduce structure/zeros of counting functions Sn(r).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition form for Sn(r) (Proposition 4.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed n there exist polynomials Pn(r) and Qn(r) such that Sn(r) = Pn(r) + (−1)^r Qn(r). Also Sn(r) satisfies a list of vanishing relations at integer points analogous to Hn(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from generating function Gn(λ) and the denominator factors coming from CF(E) structure. Small Gn(λ) examples are given to illustrate the form and to compute small values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationality bridge: integer solutions ↔ rational points (Lemma 4.6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonzero vector (γ,t) ∈ N^{m+1} belongs to the monoid E_P (encoding scaled integer solutions) iff γ/t is a rational point of the rational convex polytope P (with t>0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This translates counting of integer/rational points into counting lattice points in a homogeneous system; it is the key combinatorial encoding that links Ehrhart theory to generating functions of monoids.

rubrics_metrics.name: CF(E_P) description via vertices (Lemma 4.6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rational convex polytope P with vertex set V, the completely fundamental elements CF(E_P) are exactly the vectors ((den α)α, den α) for vertices α ∈ V (den α denotes the denominator of α in lowest terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the exact denominator factors (1−λ^{den α}) appearing in the generating function for E_P and is used to determine orders of poles and quasiperiods of Ehrhart quasipolynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational generating function and poles for Ehrhart series (Theorem 4.6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rational convex d-polytope P, the generating function F(P,λ)=Σ i(P,n) λ^n is a rational function whose denominator can be taken as ∏_{α∈V} (1−λ^{den α}). The pole at λ=1 has order d+1, and i(P,n) (and ¯i(P,n)) are quasipolynomials of degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: translate to monoid generating function E_P(x,y), apply previously established denominator description, and analyze Laurent expansion near λ=1. Consequence: Ehrhart quasipolynomial theory (quasiperiods divide lcm of vertex denominators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity for Ehrhart quasipolynomials (Theorem 4.6.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is a rational convex polytope of dimension d then ¯i(P,n) = (−1)^d i(P,−n) (reciprocity theorem), i.e., interior-counting and full-counting Ehrhart quasipolynomials are related by this sign and argument inversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from a relation on the monoid generating function E_P evaluated at (1,...,1,λ) and application of rational-function reciprocity results; standard and central to Ehrhart theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral polytope simplification (Corollary 4.6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is an integral convex d-polytope (all vertices integer) then i(P,n) and ¯i(P,n) are ordinary polynomials of degree d, satisfy i(P,0)=1, and ¯i(P,n) = (−1)^d i(P,−n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this special case den α = 1 for all vertices, so the Ehrhart series denominator simplifies to (1−λ)^{d+1} and quasipolynomial becomes polynomial. This yields computational simplifications (e.g., Birkhoff polytope Ω_n is integral).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading coefficient equals relative volume (Proposition 4.6.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integral convex d-polytope P the leading coefficient of the polynomial i(P,n) equals the relative volume ν(P) (the usual statement: leading coefficient = ν(P)/d! depending on normalization; the text relates i(P,n) asymptotically to ν(P)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: Riemann-sum/hypercube approximation argument — counting scaled integer points approximates volume; corollaries give methods to compute ν(P) from finitely many Ehrhart values and classical 2D/3D formulas are listed as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to Birkhoff and symmetric Birkhoff polytopes (Example/Proposition 4.6.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Birkhoff polytope Ω_n (doubly-stochastic matrices) is integral and its Ehrhart polynomial is Hn(r); V(Ω_n) are permutation matrices. For the symmetric case Σ_n the vertex denominators are 1 or 2, producing the Sn(r)=Pn(r)+(−1)^r Qn(r) decomposition and the conclusions from Ehrhart theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows how general Ehrhart results recover the combinatorial properties of Hn(r) and Sn(r); use vertex/CF(E) descriptions to deduce denominator/quasiperiod constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walk-counting via adjacency powers (Transfer-matrix basic principle / Theorem 4.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite weighted digraph D with adjacency matrix A, the (i,j)-entry of A^n equals A_{ij}(n), the sum of weights of all walks of length n from vertex i to j (with A^0 := I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the elementary combinatorial interpretation that underlies the transfer-matrix method: counting walks reduces to matrix powers; weights multiply along edges. Useful for encoding combinatorial constraints as digraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational generating function for walks (Theorem 4.7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generating function F_{ij}(D,λ)=Σ_{n≥0} A_{ij}(n) λ^n equals (−1)^{i+j} det(I−λA : j,i) / det(I−λA), i.e., a rational function whose denominator is det(I−λA) and whose numerator is the appropriate minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate linear-algebra derivation: F(λ)=(I−λA)^{-1}, and Cramer's rule gives the minor/determinant expression; degree bounds follow from polynomial degrees of numerator/denominator. Use to show rationality of many combinatorial generating functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-walk generating function (Corollary 4.7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q(λ)=det(I−λA) then the generating function Σ_{n≥1} CD(n) λ^n (sum over weights of closed walks of length n) equals λ Q'(λ)/Q(λ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation: trace identities and factorization via nonzero eigenvalues; yields compact formulas for cyclic-count enumerations and leads to expressions where numerator is derivative of denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral decomposition for undirected/symmetric graphs (Corollary 4.7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a real symmetric adjacency matrix A with eigenvalues λ_k and orthonormal eigenvectors u_k, (A^n)_{ij} = Σ_k (u_{ik} u_{jk}) λ_k^n. Thus walk counts are finite linear combinations of eigenvalue powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields closed-form (exponential-polynomial) expressions for walk counts and explains methods to extract asymptotics via dominant eigenvalues; coefficients c_k = u_{ik} u_{jk} are given explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encoding longer memory constraints and rationality of languages (Proposition 4.7.8 and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one forbids a finite set S of finite words (factors) over a finite alphabet, the number f(n) of words of length n avoiding S has generating function in Q(λ) (rational). If one instead counts cyclic words (indices mod n) the circular-count generating function is of the form λ Q'(λ)/Q(λ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: enlarge state space to remember required past (Markovian encoding), form a finite digraph of states, and apply transfer-matrix theorems. Examples show building vertex set as k‑tuples of previous letters and computing determinants or using initial values to determine numerator.
